solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tricky anagram by leading compiler

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward to sort out, so these letters are to be rearranged
the leading part of a word is its first letter, here of compiler

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that this anagram, set by the top compiler, is a tricky one.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme drinks have no separate definition; the whole clue builds the word. ANAGRAM plus C, the first letter of 'compiler', rearranged gives the brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a Gascon brandy, one of the many drinks filling this grid as its theme.

clue.text: Davies trained as counsel

indicators.note: trained means brought into a new shape, so the letters of Davies are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Davies has qualified as a barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counsel' looks like a noun for a lawyer, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To counsel someone is to give them guidance, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Household penning short account showing measure of intelligence

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a ménage is a household

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tale is an account or story

explanation.surface: A family's books are kept short, revealing how bright they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Household' is the French-derived ménage, and 'short' drops the final letter of the account word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental age is a psychological score comparing a person's ability with average children of each age.

clue.text: Unfinished old sailing boat in Sri Lankan city

indicators.note: unfinished means the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: a galley was an ancient ship powered by sail and oars

explanation.surface: An incomplete old ship lies in a port in Sri Lanka.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' trims GALLEY to five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Galle is a port city on the south-west coast of Sri Lanka, famous for its fort.

clue.text: Likely to forget about cinemas

indicators.note: about suggests being moved around, so the letters of cinemas are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps losing track of what is on at the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesic person suffers memory loss, so is liable to lose track of things.

clue.text: German musician on the radio

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is spoken aloud, so the musician's word is judged by sound

parts.note: a rapper is a hip-hop musician

explanation.surface: A German performer is being broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic speech RAPPER sounds like RAPPA. The theme drink has no separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian grape-pomace brandy, one of the drinks forming the puzzle's theme.

clue.text: Chairs about entrance to cabins on ships

parts.note: re means concerning, about

indicators.note: entrance to points to the opening letter of cabins

parts.note: liners are large passenger ships

explanation.surface: Deckchairs set out near the cabin doors of cruise ships.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue 'on' just places C above LINERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Recliners are armchairs whose backs tip back, a kind of seat.

clue.text: Leader's lodge

definitions.meaning: to lodge something is to insert or file it, as a complaint

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link; read as a phrase the answer splits into put plus in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian president's surname, and the phrasal verb meaning submit or insert.

clue.text: He ain't an unreliable Greek

indicators.note: unreliable suggests things not staying in place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slangy complaint that some Greek man cannot be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: An Athenian is a person from Athens, the Greek capital.

clue.text: Worried, Calvin pens advisory note

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so one piece is placed within the other
worried means agitated or shaken up, so the letters of Calvin are jumbled

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is a note telling the reader to take heed

explanation.surface: An anxious man named Calvin writes a cautionary memo.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme drinks have no separate definition; the whole clue is wordplay, with the note sitting inside the shuffled name.
explanation.definitionFit: Vin blanc is French for white wine, one of the theme's drinks.

clue.text: Sort of egg dish?

definitions.meaning: a boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs, a British picnic snack
to dish a plan is to ruin or put an end to it

explanation.surface: A query about some kind of egg-based recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like food but is the verb meaning to ruin. The drink sense, whisky, is the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the breaded egg snack, and the verb meaning thwart; also the whisky of the theme.

clue.text: Source of light to cry over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for cry is read from the bottom up

parts.note: blub is informal British for weep

explanation.surface: A lamp or sunlight brings someone to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: A light bulb is the glass part of a lamp that gives off light.

clue.text: Nothing but sandwiches

indicators.note: to sandwich something is to hold it between two layers, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: save means except, as in all save one
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A lunch order of only sandwiches, nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' is the preposition meaning except, not a conjunction. The theme drink has no separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white wine from the Veneto, one of the theme's drinks.

clue.text: Initially unavailable in southern French town

definitions.text: Initially unavailable in southern French town

indicators.note: in places one piece within another

parts.note: Avignon is a town in Provence, once seat of the popes

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the following word, unavailable

explanation.surface: Something is not to be had in a town in the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside AVIGNON after S. The theme grape has no separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauvignon is a white-wine grape and the wine made from it, part of the drinks theme.

clue.text: Bistro with wine, reportedly

parts.note: a bistro is a small eatery serving drinks, which loosely stands for a bar

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the word for wine counts by its sound

parts.note: sack is an old name for sherry-like white wine from Spain

explanation.surface: A restaurant serving wine, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK, Falstaff's favourite wine, sounds like SAC. The theme drink has no separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white wine from Bordeaux, one of the theme's drinks.

clue.text: Revised snowboarding ban removed at entrance

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters are reordered
removed means taken away, so the letters of ban come out of the pool

explanation.surface: A ski resort updates its rule banning snowboards at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: SNOWBOARDING less B, A, N leaves SOWORDING, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A swing door is one that opens both ways on hinges, used at an entrance.

clue.text: Insect's terrible fate

parts.note: a bee is an insect; the 's joins it to what follows

indicators.note: terrible suggests something badly mangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bug meets a gruesome end.
explanation.walkthrough: BEE then FATE rearranged as FTEA. The theme drink has no separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef tea is a hot savoury drink made by stewing beef, given to invalids; part of the drinks theme.

clue.text: Somewhat poor quality mixture of dirt and earth

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so these letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: Soil that is a blend of dirt and earth is not very good.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-rate means of inferior standard, below second best.

clue.text: Old reports about those who swear, it's said

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Historic accounts concerning people who curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' points to the saying 'swear like a trooper'.
explanation.definitionFit: Troopers, cavalry soldiers, are proverbial for bad language.

clue.text: His 'n' her Rolls

indicators.note: to roll is to tumble over, so the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A couple's matching Rolls-Royce cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' looks like the car, but it is the anagram signal acting on HISNHER. The theme wine has no separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenish is wine from the Rhine region, an old name for hock and part of the theme.

clue.text: Warm-up event?

parts.note: a preliminary race to qualify is a warm-up event; also warmth itself makes things warm up

explanation.walkthrough: Read two ways: a qualifying round in athletics, or the warmth that warms things up.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a heat is a qualifying round; heat also means warmth.

clue.text: Contralto sitting in Nice

parts.note: C is a standard abbreviation for contralto in musical scores
assis is French for seated, and Nice is a French city

explanation.surface: A singer with a low voice takes a seat on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, telling us to use French. The theme drink has no separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassis is a blackcurrant liqueur, part of the drinks theme.

clue.text: Free from sin, is inclined to enter church

indicators.note: to enter means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
leans means is inclined, as to one side

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to go into a church to be absolved.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse a soul is to purify it, removing guilt.

clue.text: Eye's funny, not opening

definitions.note: the possessive stands for the adjective, of the eye

indicators.note: not opening means the first letter of the word is left off

parts.note: jocular means joking, funny

explanation.surface: Something about an eye looks odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye's' defines an adjective: belonging to the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocular means relating to the eye or vision.

clue.text: Agreed on a review

indicators.note: a review looks again at something, so these letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A committee settles on revisiting a matter.
explanation.walkthrough: AGREEDONA rearranged; the theme drink has no separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a fizzy orange-flavoured soft drink, part of the theme.

clue.text: Well over half of England's characters could be obtuse

indicators.note: characters means letters, here taken as a set to be rearranged
well over half of means the first five of the seven letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Many English people are said to be rather slow on the uptake.
explanation.walkthrough: The first five letters of ENGLAND, ENGLA, rearranged. The Angles gave England its name.
explanation.definitionFit: An obtuse angle is one between 90 and 180 degrees, so an example of the type.

clue.text: Pompous dwarf's question about his identity?

definitions.text: Pompous dwarf's question about his identity?

parts.words: Pompous dwarf's question about his identity?
parts.note: one of Snow White's seven dwarfs is called Doc, the bossy one

explanation.surface: A self-important little man checks who he is.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'Me, Doc?', a question Snow White's dwarf Doc might ask. The theme wine has no separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red Bordeaux wine from the region of that name, part of the theme.

clue.text: Groundsman's machine destroyed more around wicket

indicators.note: around means wrapped about the other piece
destroyed means broken up, so the letters of more are rearranged

parts.note: W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket groundsman's machine has wrecked more of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: MORE rearranged as MOER wraps W.
explanation.definitionFit: A mower is the machine a groundsman uses to cut grass.

clue.text: Went back, holding children's horse, we hear

definitions.text: Went back, holding children's horse, we hear

indicators.note: holding means having one piece inside another
back means the word for went is read from its end

parts.note: went means departed, gone

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: gee-gee is nursery talk for a horse

explanation.surface: Someone returned riding a toy pony.
explanation.walkthrough: GONE turned backwards gives ENOG, which holds GG: GEE-GEE said aloud as the letters G G. The theme drink has no separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a drink of beaten eggs, milk and often spirit, part of the theme.

clue.text: This children's fight can escalate rapidly

definitions.meaning: a winter battle between children throwing packed handfuls of frozen flakes
as a verb, something that grows faster and faster as it rolls along

explanation.surface: A playground scrap that quickly gets out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink, advocaat with lemonade, is the theme sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses of the word: the winter fight and the verb for rapid growth, plus a cocktail in the theme.

clue.text: Small German gentleman at end of party

definitions.text: Small German gentleman at end of party

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Herr is the German title for a man, like Mister

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of the following word, party

explanation.surface: A short German man lingers at the close of a party.
explanation.walkthrough: S + HERR + Y; the theme drink has no separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from Jerez in Spain, part of the drinks theme.

clue.text: Almost close at hand all the time

definitions.text: Almost close at hand all the time

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: nearby means close at hand
e'er is the poetic short form of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Something is nearly within reach, constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: NEARBY loses its last letter to give NEARB, then E'ER. The theme drink has no separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Near beer is low-alcohol beer, a drink in the theme.
